headline: Large Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of grid infrastructure upgrades and capacity procurement, rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger (with amendments)
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users
news_headline: Virginia Legislature Bucks Governor's Amendments to Dominion-Backed Bill
news_summary: This article details how HB 1393, along with SB 253, aims to assign certain electric grid upgrade costs to data centers, potentially saving typical residential customers $5.52 a month while increasing data center bills by 15%. It also mentions that the legislature rejected some of Governor Spanberger's suggested amendments that would have weakened the explicit cost-shift mechanism.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water consumed by these facilities to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger (via Executive Order 22)
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden)
news_headline: As They Consider New Data Centers, States Target Water Use
news_summary: This article discusses how states, including Virginia with HB 496 and SB 553, are increasingly focusing on data center water consumption. It highlights that these bills require water suppliers to report the volumes of potable and reclaimed water delivered to data centers, aiming for greater transparency and planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine their sound profile on nearby residential units and schools, and grants localities more authority over siting.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul
opponents: Data center developers (due to potential restrictions and increased assessment requirements)
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: This article explains that HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on homes and schools within 500 feet. It also clarifies that while the law mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
